history.period: 1620-1628 (per Incredible India; reported via travel sources)
history.summary: The hilltop Karni Mata temple stands on the Machla Magra hills near Doodh Talai Lake, close to the city centre. Built by Maharana Karan Singh between 1620 and 1628, the small white-stone shrine enshrines a stone idol of Karni Mata; the 'Manshapurna' name reflects the belief that heartfelt wishes (mansha) made here are fulfilled. FLAG: this is NOT the famous Deshnoke rat temple near Bikaner - Incredible India explicitly distinguishes the two. The Mansapurna Karni Mata Ropeway (built 2008, described as Rajasthan's first ropeway) runs from Deendayal Upadhyay Park to the hilltop in about 5 minutes; the summit offers 360-degree views of Lake Pichola, the City Palace and the Aravalli hills, making it a popular sunset point. Coordinates from map geocode (24.56693, 73.68523); Wikipedia publishes 24.56586, 73.68830.

name: Karni Mata Temple, Udaipur
town_description: Udaipur, the 'City of Lakes' in southern Rajasthan, was founded as the capital of the Mewar kingdom by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Set among the Aravalli hills around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, it is one of India's most visited heritage cities, known for its palaces, temples and old-city lanes.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 24 km away.
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 4 km away.
travel.road: Near Doodh Talai Lake in the city centre; reached on foot up the hill steps or via the ropeway from Deendayal Upadhyay Park (ropeway approx 9:00 AM-9:00 PM; charges vary across sources, roughly Rs 110-150 return - verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; late afternoon/sunset is popular for the panoramic views.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: one lists temple 4:00 AM-10:00 AM and 5:00 PM-9:00 PM, another lists 4:00 AM-7:30 PM (Incredible India) - verify on arrival.
